commit_subject: Repair New Jersey 2026 resident income tax core
description: Independent review required repairs for gambling/lottery losses and thresholds, valid MFS credit/property paths, caller-completed legal-result inputs, the shared-responsibility boundary, blanket-oracle claims, material threshold coverage, service/housing overlap, direct credit assertions, and malformed YAML descriptions.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Inside the profile it claimed to support, the module added raw `nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` straight into New Jersey gross income with no representation of N.J.S.54A:6-11 (which excludes New Jersey Lottery winnings except from a single prize exceeding $10,000) and no within-category offset of same-year wagering losses that 54A:5-2 permits, so a resident with, say, a $5,000 New Jersey Lottery prize was taxed on an amount the statute excludes from gross income.
triage.triage_notes: Read the provisions through the pinned corpus: 54A:6-11 is verbatim "Gross income shall not include lottery winnings from the New Jersey Lottery, except that New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income"; 54A:5-1(g) is bare "Gambling winnings" and 54A:5-2 allows within-category loss offsets; 54A:3-3(c) lists the three disallowances (household/dependent care, excluded MSA distributions, self-employed health insurance) the fix now encodes; 54A:3A-17(c)/(d) give the title-interest proportion and the MFS tenants-by-entirety one-half share; 54A:4-17(c) reads "Married couples shall file a joint return in order to claim the credit" with the section 21(e)(3)/(4) exception the fix adds. Pre-fix citation list did not even contain 54a:6-11, 54a:11-3, or 54a:11-4. This is a multi-defect repair round and one kind had to be chosen: unrepresented_clause covers the largest group (missing lottery exclusion and loss netting, missing 54A:3-3(c) disallowances, missing MFS half-share and title-interest proportion, missing CDCC married-living-apart exception, missing 54A:4-17.1 joint-return bar). Two other findings arguably fall elsewhere: the new `nj_pit_2026_service_remuneration_excludes_employer_housing_value` guard fixes a double-count (employer-furnished housing was both inside total service remuneration and added again as its own gross-income term), and the new 54A:11-3/11-4 typed hold plus `nj_pit_2026_total_return_tax_liability` deferred output is a wrong_entity_or_scope-style correction (the net output was presented as a return-level candidate without the separate State shared responsibility tax). Note the remedy for gambling/alimony/exempt-interest/qualified-fund facts is removal plus a typed hold rather than encoding the clause, so the post-fix module is narrower; the pre-fix defect is still real because those facts were inside the claimed supported profile and produced a wrong number. The commit body is empty, so the quote is from the PR body. The five-way split of `nj_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` into filing/income/deferred-income/deduction/property sub-rules is structural, not itself a defect. Follow-up commit 15f982991 "Complete New Jersey credit boundary coverage" in the same PR also touches this file; the PR records the final reviewed head as 15f982991ad36e24a6472d1a03c9ce0a640d5d4c. PR has no review or comment records in the bundle (reviews/review_comments/issue_comments all empty), so the findings list in the PR body is the only reviewer evidence.
triage.verifier_justification: The refutation attempts fail: the pre-fix formula really did add the input `nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` (declared as "Gross gambling winnings in the supported profile") straight into `nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_gross_income`, its only exception proof atom was 54A:6-14 (interest on obligations), and 54A:6-11 appeared in the pre-fix header only under `upstream_source_check.checked_paths`, never in `corpus_citation_paths` or any rule — so the exclusion was demonstrably unrepresented, and the pre-fix `supported_profile_applies` gate contained no gambling or lottery condition. Read through the pinned release, 54A:6-11 says "Gross income shall not include lottery winnings from the New Jersey Lottery, except that New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income", and 54A:5-2 permits same-category offsets, while 54A:5-1(g) makes "Gambling winnings" a category of its own — so gross receipts with no exclusion and no same-year wagering-loss offset overstated gross income against the source. The one real counter-argument, that the pre-fix caller flag `nj_pit_2026_has_specialty_income_exclusion_or_deduction` ("any unencoded Title 54A chapter 3 or 6 specialty exclusion or deduction") might already have held lottery cases, does not survive: it is a caller-completed legal conclusion the module's own header disclaims, it is limited to chapters 3 and 6 so it cannot reach the chapter-5 loss netting, and no wagering-loss input existed at all. The kind holds because the term removed is grounded in 54A:5-1(g) (so not untraceable) and the repair adds the missing exception's machinery — the `nj_pit_2026_new_jersey_lottery_prize_exclusion_limit` parameter at 10000 with the 54A:6-11 excerpt, a per-prize judgment input, and a gross-receipts/losses split.
triage.verifier_notes: Decisive evidence spans three places in the diff: the removal `-          + nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` from rules[nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_gross_income].versions[0].formula; the new parameter `+  - name: nj_pit_2026_new_jersey_lottery_prize_exclusion_limit` with `+      - {effective_from: '2026-01-01', effective_to: '2026-12-31', formula: '10000'}` and excerpt "New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income"; and the new gate line `+          and not nj_pit_2026_has_gambling_or_new_jersey_lottery_activity` in nj_pit_2026_no_deferred_income_branch_applies. Two caveats for a reviewer. (1) The remedy is a typed hold (deferral) plus a threshold parameter rather than encoding the exclusion arithmetic, so a reviewer who reads "the fix adds it" strictly could prefer wrong_entity_or_scope (the supported population was re-scoped); I judge unrepresented_clause better because the pre-fix output disagreed with 54A:6-11/54A:5-2 for taxpayers the module claimed to support, and the fix does add representation of the $10,000 boundary. (2) This commit is a bundle: the same formula also lost `- nj_pit_2026_exempt_us_or_nj_obligation_interest`, `- nj_pit_2026_exempt_qualified_investment_fund_dividends`, and `+ nj_pit_2026_alimony_received` (removal of caller-completed legal classifications), and the commit separately repairs MFS property/credit halving (new nj_pit_2026_mfs_property_benefit_share = 0.5 citing "shall each be entitled to one-half of the deduction"), medical-expense disallowances (new nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_allowable_medical_expenses), and the 54A:11-3 shared-responsibility-tax boundary. If the corpus wants one defect per module change, this file supports several distinct fidelity entries; the gambling/lottery one is the best evidenced. Statutes read through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix (corpus commit 01e00777cb), fix_time_corpus_match=same_body. Incidental tooling note: two sequential `git show` redirects chained with && into the scratchpad produced truncated/mixed files on the first attempt; re-running each show separately gave the correct 1654-line pre-image.
